instr: New words: learn four made-up words and what they mean, then answer questions about them.
clue: You will see four made-up words, each with its meaning, for a few seconds each. Learn them. Then answer 8 questions: pick the meaning of a word, or pick the word that fits a new example. Click or tap an answer, or press 1-4. Press Start when ready.
meanings: a tool for opening jars with stuck lids
the tiredness you feel after a very long phone call
a person who waters other people's plants while they are away
a short walk taken right after a meal
a cloth bag used only for carrying bread
rain that falls while the sun is shining
a drawer full of things nobody uses
a small lamp worn on the head for reading in bed
the fresh smell of a room right after cleaning
a game played to pass the time while waiting in a queue
a note left under a parked car's windscreen wiper
the sudden worry that you left something switched on at home
a cup that keeps tea hot for hours
a bare track made by people walking across grass
a tune that stays in your head all day
a box with small sections for sorting screws by size
examples: The lid of the jam would not turn until Deniz used one.
After talking to her aunt for two hours, Elif felt drained and could not think.
While the family was on holiday, a neighbour came every day to keep their flowers alive.
After dinner, Murat went once around the block before sitting down again.
At the bakery, Selin put the warm loaves into one she had brought from home.
The sky was bright and sunny, yet drops were falling on the street.
Old keys, broken pens and dead batteries all ended up in one in the kitchen.
So as not to wake his brother, Can put one on to read at night.
When the floors were washed and the windows opened, the whole flat had it.
To make the time at the bank go faster, the children played one.
When she came back to the car park, there was a message for her on the glass.
On the bus, Ali suddenly thought the stove might still be on.
Three hours after pouring, the tea in Ayla's mug was still steaming.
Students cut across the lawn so often that the grass there disappeared in a line.
Emre kept humming the same melody from the morning radio until bedtime.
Every small compartment held screws of only one length.
